title: Agricultural Engineer in the Philippines: Course, Board Exam, Jobs and Pay
metaTitle: Agricultural Engineer: Course, Board Exam, Jobs and Pay
metaDescription: How to become an agricultural engineer in the Philippines: the ABE course, the PRC board exam under RA 10915, who is hiring, the pay, and technician roles.
excerpt: An agricultural engineer designs the irrigation, machines, buildings and processing systems that farms run on. In the Philippines the profession is now called agricultural and biosystems engineering, and it has its own law, board exam and license. This guide covers the course, the exam, the jobs and the pay. It also covers the technician roles that work beside the engineers.

heroImage.alt: A tractor working a field, the kind of farm machinery an agricultural engineer designs and manages

blocks.text:
Republic Act 10915 lists the work in detail. An agricultural and biosystems engineer designs, builds and supervises irrigation and drainage, soil and water conservation, farm power and machinery, and farm buildings. The same scope covers post harvest and processing facilities, renewable energy and farm electrification, and farm waste management. It even includes weather systems for farms, automation and farm information systems.

In plain terms, if water, a machine, a dryer or a warehouse is involved, an engineer signs off on it. For example, a small farm reservoir, a combine harvester and a rice mill layout all fall under the profession.

The agricultural engineer course today is the Bachelor of Science in Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering, or BSABE. It grew out of the older BS Agricultural Engineering, and RA 10915 also lets BSAE graduates take the board exam under the terms it sets. The Commission on Higher Education sets the curriculum with the Board of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering. State universities offer the program, and UP Los Baños runs it through its Institute of Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering.

Expect a heavy load of math and engineering, plus farm science. The board exam subjects give a good picture of what you will study:

items: Agricultural and biosystems power, energy and machinery, including machine design and farm mechanization
Land and water resources engineering, including irrigation, drainage, soil and water conservation and aquaculture engineering
Agricultural and biosystems structures and environment, including farm buildings and forest engineering
Agricultural and bioprocess engineering, including cold storage, farm electricity and food processing
Project management, feasibility studies, research and extension
Farm, fishery, ecological and environmental sciences, math, basic engineering, laws and ethics

blocks.text: RA 10915, the Philippine Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering Act of 2016, became law on July 21, 2016 and replaced RA 8559. It requires every agricultural and biosystems engineer to pass a licensure exam given through the Professional Regulation Commission. Only licensed engineers may hold posts with engineering duties in government and in private firms.

items.title: Finish the degree
items.text: Graduate with a BS in Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering, or a BS in Agricultural Engineering, from a school recognized by CHED.

items.title: Check that you qualify
items.text: You must be of good moral character. You must also be a Filipino citizen, or a citizen of a country that lets Filipinos practice there.

items.title: Take the PRC board exam
items.text: Apply through the PRC for the licensure exam for agricultural and biosystems engineers. Check the PRC schedule for the current exam dates.

items.title: Pass with the required grades
items.text: You need a weighted general average of 70 percent, with no subject below 55 percent. If your average passes but a subject falls below 55, you retake only that subject.

items.title: Register and keep learning
items.text: Once registered, you join the accredited professional organization and complete continuing professional development to keep your license.

blocks.text: Agricultural engineer hiring: who needs you

The law itself creates demand. Section 34 of RA 10915 covers agencies, local governments and state universities that run irrigation, mechanization, post harvest or farm to market road programs. It tells them to employ the engineers they need. It also requires at least one licensed engineer in many facilities and firms. As a result, agricultural engineer hiring reaches well beyond the Department of Agriculture.

blocks.caption: Where agricultural engineers work, based on RA 10915
rows: Mechanization, irrigation and farm infrastructure programs
Engineer posts in agriculture offices, farm projects, inspections
Design, operation and maintenance of irrigation
At least one licensed engineer for installation, sales and service
Rice mills, feed mills, sugar mills, food plants
Checking irrigation, post harvest and processing projects
Irrigation, farm to market roads, farm structures

blocks.text: Demand also follows the wider farm sector, which still employs about one in five working Filipinos. Our page on [agriculture in the Philippine economy](/blog/agriculture-in-the-philippine-economy) has the latest PSA numbers.

Pay depends a lot on the employer, the region and your experience, and public data is thin. PayScale's 2026 page for agricultural engineers in the Philippines shows an average base salary of PHP 457,800 a year. That is about PHP 38,150 a month. Its middle range runs from about PHP 250,000 to PHP 1,000,000 a year. But the figure rests on only 11 salary profiles, last updated in December 2024, so treat it as a rough guide.

In government, pay follows the salary grade of each position under the Salary Standardization Law. Executive Order 64 of 2024 set the current salary schedule for civilian government workers. Since the grade differs from one engineer post to another, check the salary grade printed on each job posting before you apply.
Agricultural technician and agricultural equipment technician roles

Not every farm job needs a license. An agricultural technician works in the field: scouting pests, checking crop stages, calibrating sprayers, collecting samples and keeping records. Many start with an agriculture degree or a short course, and they often work under an agriculturist or an engineer.

An agricultural equipment technician keeps the machines running. That means tractors, hand tractors, harvesters, dryers, pumps and threshers. RA 10915 asks TESDA to set competency standards and training for agricultural and biosystems engineering technicians and operators. So this path usually runs through TESDA training rather than a board exam. Also, since every machinery firm must have a licensed engineer, technicians and engineers often work side by side in the same shop.
How anee.io's AI agricultural technician supports field teams

Engineers and technicians spend much of their day answering the same field questions. So anee.io gives every farm [Anee, an AI agricultural technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician). Anee answers in Tagalog or English and reads the farm's cropping schedule, each lot's growth stage and the weather first. It can look at a photo of a pest or a sick plant, and it can write a full season report.

For the team itself, anee.io keeps the plan and the people in one place. The [cropping calendar](/features/cropping-calendar) dates every task from each lot's own day zero. The [workers and payroll](/features/farm-workers-and-payroll) module assigns hands to activities and sends a 6 AM email of the day's plan. Each worker also gets a login with view or edit rights. Meanwhile, [farm maps](/features/farm-maps) let you draw and measure fields over satellite imagery.

blocks.title: Build a record while you study
blocks.text: Students and new graduates can plan a sample season on a real field, log each activity and write a season report. A clean record of a real crop is useful proof of field experience when you apply.

blocks.text: Questions about becoming an agricultural engineer

items.q: What course do I take to become an agricultural engineer?
items.a: Take a Bachelor of Science in Agricultural and Biosystems Engineering. Graduates of the older BS Agricultural Engineering may also qualify for the board exam under the terms of RA 10915.

items.q: What is the passing rate of the agricultural engineer board exam?
items.a: You need a weighted general average of at least 70 percent, with no subject below 55 percent. A student who passes the average but falls below 55 in a subject retakes only that subject.

items.q: How much does an agricultural engineer earn in the Philippines?
items.a: PayScale's 2026 page gives an average base salary of about PHP 457,800 a year, based on a small sample. Government posts pay by salary grade, which each job posting states.
The Department of Agriculture, local governments, irrigation systems, machinery firms, rice and feed mills, banks that lend to agribusiness, consultancies and universities.

items.q: Is an agricultural technician the same as an agricultural engineer?
items.a: No. A technician does field and machine work and is usually trained through a degree, a short course or TESDA. An engineer holds a PRC license and signs off on designs and projects.
